newsitem.title: USA: Blue-chip stocks extend their rally.
newsitem.headline: Blue-chip stocks extend their rally.

text.p: Blue chips climbed anew Thursday, as Wall Street showed no letup in its appetite for stocks amid a fresh batch of solid corporate earnings.

At 1 p.m. EDT (1700 GMT), the 30-stock Dow was up 19.75 points at 8,058.63, one day after closing above the 8,000 milestone for the first time. The market was initially dragged lower by profit-taking.
But in the broader market, declining issues led advances by a small margin on heavy volume of 370 million shares on the New York Stock Exchange.
The Nasdaq composite index slipped 2.03 points to 1,578.60, pausing after racking up 10 straight record closes.

"It seems impossible to hold this market back," said Sam Stovall, an analyst at Standard & Poor's Industry reports. "In general, investors are very opmistic about the outlook for interest rates and the outlook for earnings."
The jump in the blue chips coincided with gains in the bond market.
The benchmark 30-year Treasury bond was up 9/32, or $2.81 on a $1,000 bond, lowering its yield to 6.46 percent from Wednesday's close of 6.48 percent.
Merck & Co., a Dow component, jumped 7-1/4 to 105-3/4 after it reported better-than-forecast results.
Fast-food giant McDonald's Corp., another Dow component, also gained after it posted strong quarterly earnings. Its stock was up 14/16 at 50-15/16.
Sears, Roebuck & Co. rose 2-3/8 to 58-7/8 after it reported upbeat results.
"Earnings, by and large, have been good," said Dick Stein, vice president of U.S. Clearing Corp.
In addition, the outlook for the economy could not be rosier, analysts said.

"We are nervous about valuations, but given the continued outlook for low inflation, moderate growth and prospects for lower interest rates, the stock market has just mushroomed here," said Harvey Hirshhorn, Stein Roe and Farnham chief economist and investment strategist.
Technology stocks did not fare as well as blue-chip companies, pausing after recent surges.
"These companies have had a huge run so they are entitled to pull back here," Stein said. "Groups are playing catch-up. It's rotational."
The high-tech sector awaited quarterly results from Microsoft Corp., which were due after the close.
Woolworth Corp. gained 2 to 37-1/16 after it announced plans to close its more than 400 five-and-dime stores in the United States.
